answer.origin: Motley Fool article by Robert Izquierdo, published 2026-08-01 (third-party media view). The article says its revenue data come from company filings as of July 31, 2026. Its Alphabet Q2 claims (Google Cloud revenue of $24.8B, up 82% year over year, and backlog above $500B, up from $462B in Q1) are secondhand and not verified against Alphabet's filing in this record.
answer.note: For NVDA, this source is mainly context, not a company-specific fact. Its Alphabet Google Cloud figures (Q2 revenue $24.8B, up 82% year over year; backlog up from $462B in Q1 to over $500B) indicate strong reported demand for AI cloud services at a major hyperscaler. Read conditionally, that supports the view that AI infrastructure demand remained strong into mid-2026, which is the demand channel that matters for Nvidia. The article also states Alphabet is among Nvidia's customers, which places Alphabet on the NVDA demand side. The article gives no Alphabet purchase amount, so the Google Cloud figures do not show Nvidia orders or Alphabet's share of Nvidia revenue. The Nvidia data in the article are a third-party report of company figures: most recent quarter revenue of $81.6B (quarter ended April 2026), and a forecast of about $91B for the next quarter, tied by the article to the Vera Rubin platform. The forecast is company guidance as reported by a third party and should be checked against Nvidia's own release before it is relied on. The article's quarterly revenue table mixes Nvidia and Alphabet series and cannot be read as a clean Nvidia history, so it is not used here.
limitations: The article does not disclose the dollar amount or share of Nvidia revenue attributable to Alphabet, so the Alphabet customer relationship carries no quantified Nvidia exposure.
The Google Cloud revenue and backlog figures are Alphabet figures, reported secondhand by a media article; the backlog definition and period-end basis are not stated.
The $91B next-quarter Nvidia figure is a forecast reported by a third party; the article does not give the guidance date, its assumptions, or confirm it against Nvidia's filing.
The article's quarterly table combines Nvidia and Alphabet series with unlabeled per-company values, so it cannot be used to verify Nvidia's quarterly revenue path.
The timing and revenue contribution of the Vera Rubin platform are described only as expected by the article and are not quantified.
follow_up: Check Nvidia's earnings release or 10-Q for the quarter ended April 26, 2026, to confirm the $81.6B revenue figure and the next-quarter outlook of about $91B and its date.
Check Nvidia's latest 10-Q customer concentration disclosure for whether Alphabet is named as a direct customer above the reporting threshold and, if so, its percentage of revenue.
Check Alphabet's Q2 2026 10-Q or earnings release for Google Cloud revenue, the growth rate, and the backlog figure and definition, to confirm the secondhand figures.
